sections.title: Reflection and Transmission Measurement
body: The right TANGO II configuration comes down to one question: is your sample solid or liquid?

Reflection is built for solids and semi-solids. A gold-coated integrating sphere captures diffuse reflection, and sample rotators enlarge the effective measurement area, which matters for a heterogeneous sample where one 10 mm spot wouldn't represent the whole. Transmission is built for liquids, with a heater and cooler built in as standard, holding the sample between +20°C and +80°C while a dedicated sensor tracks vial temperature continuously.

faqs.question: What is the MPA III FT-NIR Spectrometer used for?
faqs.answer: The MPA III is a modular FT-NIR solution used for both sophisticated calibration method development and routine QA/QC, across food, pharmaceutical, chemical, and polymer industries.

faqs.question: What sampling modules does the MPA III support?
faqs.answer: Four: a Sample Compartment for liquids, an Integrating Sphere for solids and semi-solids, Fiber Optic Probes for measuring directly in containers, and an External Transmission Unit for automated vial or tablet analysis.

faqs.question: Can I try different sampling methods before committing to one?
faqs.answer: Yes. The modular design is built for exactly this, since the best sampling method often isn't obvious until you've tested it on your actual sample.

faqs.question: What is the warranty on the MPA III?
faqs.answer: 10 years on the interferometer's moving parts and the solid-state laser.

faqs.question: Is the MPA III suitable for a regulated pharmaceutical environment?
faqs.answer: Yes. OPUS software offers GMP and 21 CFR Part 11 compliance in validated mode, with a complete audit trail and the OPUS Validation Program covering OQ and PQ protocols to USP, JP, and Ph. Eur. guidelines.

faqs.question: Can the MPA III be used outside the lab?
faqs.answer: Yes. Its robustness supports use on the factory floor, and it can be mounted on a utility cart for mobile applications.

faqs.question: What software is available for the MPA III?
faqs.answer: OPUS/LAB for routine analysis, OPUS/IDENT for raw material identification, OPUS/CONFO for conformity checking, OPUS/QUANT2 for multivariate calibration development, and ONET for managing a network of solutions remotely.

faqs.question: Does the MPA III require trained operators?
faqs.answer: No. Customizable workspaces and guided measurement modes in OPUS are designed so untrained personnel can operate the solution from day one.

faqs.question: How is the instrument monitored for accuracy?
faqs.answer: An online diagnostic system continuously monitors all optical components and notifies the user immediately if anything falls out of specification.

faqs.question: What is the difference between the MPA III and TANGO II?
faqs.answer: The MPA III offers four interchangeable sampling modules and a full software suite for method development, while the TANGO II is a simpler, fixed-configuration analyzer built for fast, routine measurement with minimal setup.

faqs.answer: The price depends on the sampling modules and software packages your application needs. Contact Inkarp for a quotation once your requirements are confirmed.

sections.title: Sampling Modules and Method Development
sections.tabSummary: Matching a module to your sample and location
body: The right sampling method depends on the sample and where it sits, and the MPA III is built so you don't have to guess correctly the first time.

Liquids in cuvettes or disposable vials go through the Sample Compartment, with an optional heater and automated background capability. Solids and semi-solids go through the Integrating Sphere by diffuse reflection, with a sample rotator improving reproducibility on heterogeneous material. Samples that can't come to the instrument, like material sitting in a warehouse, are measured directly through Fiber Optic Probes, with two probes running at once for solids and liquids together. Tablets or vials needing automated, repeatable transmission measurements run through the External Transmission Unit with its optional sample wheel.

cta.description: The MPA III lets you test sampling methods before committing, backed by a 10-year warranty on its interferometer and laser, and a software suite that scales from routine QC to full method development. Tell us your samples and your workflow, and Inkarp will confirm the right configuration.
cta.label: Request Quote

longForm.heroHook: Try every sampling method first. Keep the one that works.
heroParagraphs: Choosing the right sampling method usually isn't obvious until you've tried it. Most solutions make you commit before you know.
The MPA III doesn't. Its modular design takes four different sampling approaches on the same solution, so you can test methods and keep the one that actually fits your sample.

Liquids in cuvettes or vials, solids and semi-solids by diffuse reflection, samples measured directly in a warehouse container, or automated tablets and vials in transmission. Swap the module, not the solution.
It's built for both jobs at once: sophisticated calibration method development, and routine QA/QC simple enough for untrained staff to run from day one.
And it's built to last. Ten years of warranty cover the interferometer's moving parts and the solid-state laser.
longForm.statsIntro: The quick stats of the MPA III FT-NIR Spectrometer cover its modular sampling design, software depth, and warranty.
